question: Where was the first meeting of the Employment Working Group of G20 conducted?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jodhpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first meeting of the Employment Working Group of G20 was conducted in **Jodhpur**.
 
• The G20 Employment Working Group addresses global employment and labor market challenges.
 
• The meeting aims to foster international cooperation and policy coordination on employment issues.
 
• It focuses on creating inclusive labor markets and promoting decent work for all.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G20 (Group of Twenty)**

 
 
• The G20 is an international forum for governments and central bank governors from 19 countries and the European Union (EU).
 
• It was established in 1999 in response to the financial crises of the late 1990s.
 
• The G20 aims to discuss policy issues that are critical to the global economy, including international financial stability, climate change mitigation, and sustainable development.
 
• The member countries include Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, South Korea, Turkey, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the European Union.
 
 
 
• **Employment Working Group (EWG)**
 
 
• The EWG is one of the working groups within the G20 framework.
 
• It focuses on employment and labor market issues and aims to promote inclusive growth and decent work.
 
• The EWG discusses various topics including job creation, workforce development, labor market policies, and social protection.
 
• It works towards achieving the G20's goal of stronger, sustainable, and balanced growth by addressing employment challenges.
